_comment: PART 1 DATA. One object per CAPTCHA. Each tester edits only their own CAPTCHA's object. Every rating starts with "verified": false (shown on the site as Preliminary). After hands-on testing with VoiceOver and keyboard-only, update rating + note and set verified to true. Ratings: pass | partial | fail | untested.

captchas.name: Google reCAPTCHA v2
captchas.style: Checkbox with image-grid escalation and an audio fallback
captchas.description: An "I'm not a robot" checkbox. If Google's risk check is unsure, it escalates to an image grid ("select all squares with traffic lights"), with an audio challenge as the fallback.
captchas.tools: VoiceOver (macOS), Safari/Chrome, keyboard only (mouse disabled), browser zoom 200%, axe DevTools
captchas.overall: The checkbox itself is labeled and keyboard-operable, but users who get escalated face an image grid with no text alternative and an audio fallback that is slow and error-prone.
captchas.best_for: Sites that need a familiar baseline and expect most users to pass at the checkbox step.
captchas.watch_out_for: Escalation to the image grid; the audio fallback; the verification expiring before the form is submitted.

experience.screen_reader: To be written after VoiceOver testing. Things to note: is the checkbox announced with its name and state; can you find the "Get an audio challenge" button; does the audio clip talk over VoiceOver; is the answer field labeled; how long does it take.
experience.keyboard: To be written after keyboard-only testing. Things to note: can you Tab to the checkbox and press Space; inside the image grid, can you reach every tile, Verify, and the audio button; is focus visible on every step.

claims_vs_found.claim: Google's help page describes a keyboard and screen-reader path: an audio challenge, with focus moved to the play button and to error messages, and the screen reader notified on success.
claims_vs_found.found: To be completed after testing. Earlier user reports describe the audio answer field lacking an accessible name and challenges expiring before they can be answered (WebAIM list, 2015); confirm whether that still happens.

1.1.1.note: Checkbox is labeled and an audio alternative exists, but audio success rates for blind users are low (Bigham & Cavender, 2009).

1.3.1.note: Check whether the audio challenge's instructions and answer field are programmatically linked.

1.4.4.note: Fixed-size iframe; check whether the image grid stays usable at 200% zoom.

2.1.1.note: Google documents a keyboard path through the checkbox and audio challenge; confirm the image grid tiles are reachable.

2.2.1.note: Verification expires after a set time with no way to extend it; audio challenges can expire mid-answer.

2.4.7.note: Past audits report weak focus visibility inside the challenge widget; confirm.

2.5.8.note: Measure the checkbox and the grid's icon buttons (reload, audio, info).

3.3.8.note: Image recognition falls under a WCAG exception, but the audio transcription does not; no puzzle-free path unless the site adds one.

4.1.2.note: Checkbox name and checked state should be announced; check the audio answer field's name.

captchas.name: hCaptcha
captchas.style: Image labeling, with an accessibility option
captchas.description: A checkbox that usually leads to image-labeling tasks. It offers two accessibility routes: a text-based challenge (only if the site owner enables it) and an accessibility cookie users register for by email.
captchas.tools: VoiceOver (macOS), Safari/Chrome, keyboard only (mouse disabled), browser zoom 200%, axe DevTools
captchas.overall: Accessibility depends on options outside the user's control (the site owner enabling the text challenge) or on a cookie that requires email registration and cross-site cookies.
captchas.best_for: Sites willing to enable the text-based accessibility challenge.
captchas.watch_out_for: The accessibility cookie breaking under browsers that block cross-site cookies (Safari by default); image challenges with no alternative when the text challenge is off.

experience.screen_reader: To be written after VoiceOver testing. Things to note: is the menu with the accessibility option reachable and announced; is the text challenge offered on the demo; does the accessibility cookie work in Safari with default settings.
experience.keyboard: To be written after keyboard-only testing. Things to note: can you reach and select image tiles with the keyboard; does any challenge variant require dragging.

claims_vs_found.claim: hCaptcha says users can choose a text-based Accessibility Challenge from the widget menu when the site enables it, or register for an accessibility cookie that lets them pass automatically or get a text challenge.
claims_vs_found.found: To be completed after testing. User reports (AppleVis) say the cookie lasts about 24 hours and requires turning on cross-site cookies in Safari; check both routes.

1.1.1.note: A non-visual route exists only if the site enables the text challenge or the user has registered for the cookie.

1.3.1.note: Check that the challenge prompt is associated with the tiles or text field.

1.4.4.note: Check whether the challenge popup fits and stays usable at 200% zoom.

2.1.1.note: Check keyboard access to every tile and to the accessibility menu.

2.2.1.note: Check whether challenges time out and whether that can be extended.

2.4.7.note: Check focus visibility on tiles and menu items.

2.5.7.note: Some challenge variants ask users to drag a piece; check whether there's a non-drag option.

2.5.8.note: Measure the checkbox, tiles and menu button.

3.3.8.note: The cookie gives a puzzle-free path, but only after email registration and with cross-site cookies allowed.

4.1.2.note: Check what VoiceOver announces for the checkbox, tiles and menu.

captchas.name: Cloudflare Turnstile
captchas.description: Runs checks on browser signals and behavior in the background. Users usually see a widget that verifies on its own, or a checkbox to click; there is no image or audio puzzle.
captchas.tools: VoiceOver (macOS), Safari/Chrome, keyboard only (mouse disabled), browser zoom 200%, axe DevTools
captchas.overall: With no puzzle, most criteria are easy to meet. The main risk is a false positive (privacy browsers, VPNs, assistive tech) that leaves the user stuck with no alternative.
captchas.best_for: Most sign-up, login and contact forms.
captchas.watch_out_for: Users blocked with no fallback when the check fails; the widget needs JavaScript.

experience.screen_reader: To be written after VoiceOver testing. Things to note: is the widget's status (verifying, success, failure) announced; is the checkbox, if shown, labeled.
experience.keyboard: To be written after keyboard-only testing. Things to note: can you Tab to and activate the checkbox; is focus visible; what happens on failure.

claims_vs_found.claim: Cloudflare's developer docs state that Turnstile is WCAG 2.2 AA compliant; a 2026 redesign aimed for WCAG 2.2 AAA.
claims_vs_found.found: To be completed after testing. The compliance claim is self-declared; no independent audit was found.

1.1.1.note: No visual puzzle; confirm the widget has a text label.

1.3.1.note: Confirm status messages are linked to the widget.

2.1.1.note: Confirm the checkbox (when shown) is keyboard-operable.

2.2.1.note: No user task to time; check whether a token expiry forces a redo.

2.4.7.note: Confirm a visible focus ring on the checkbox.

4.1.2.note: Community reports of screen-reader issues before the 2026 redesign; confirm the status changes are announced.

captchas.name: Slider / puzzle CAPTCHA (GeeTest v4)
captchas.description: Asks users to drag a slider so a puzzle piece fits its slot. It judges both where the piece ends up and how the drag moves. GeeTest says it also offers a voice verification option.
captchas.tools: VoiceOver (macOS), Safari/Chrome, keyboard only (mouse disabled), browser zoom 200%, axe DevTools
captchas.overall: The drag interaction is the barrier this audit is built around; keyboard-only and screen-reader users depend on whether the voice option exists and can be reached.
captchas.best_for: Not recommended where keyboard-only or screen-reader users are expected, unless the voice option is enabled and reachable by keyboard.
captchas.watch_out_for: Drag-only completion; the voice option being hidden or off.

experience.screen_reader: To be written after VoiceOver testing. Things to note: is the slider announced at all; is the voice verification option reachable and labeled.
experience.keyboard: To be written after keyboard-only testing. Things to note: can the slider be moved with arrow keys; can the voice option be reached with Tab.

claims_vs_found.claim: GeeTest's v4 documentation says it supports an accessibility-friendly voice verification option alongside the slide puzzle.
claims_vs_found.found: To be completed after testing. Check whether the voice option appears on the demo and works with keyboard and VoiceOver.

1.1.1.note: A voice option is claimed; confirm it exists on the demo and is labeled.

1.3.1.note: Check whether the instructions are tied to the slider control.

2.1.1.note: Drag puzzle; check whether arrow keys move the slider or the voice option is keyboard-reachable.

2.4.7.note: Check whether the slider handle shows focus.

2.5.7.note: Drag required unless the voice option is available.

3.3.8.note: No puzzle-free path unless the site adds one.

4.1.2.note: Check whether the slider has a role, name and value.
